title: Who Vouches for a Dish of Neurons?
abstract: Living neurons can now be rented through the cloud. Their operators monitor them, but nobody publishes a record of which units to trust. A culture can give poor answers, drift or die, and it cannot answer for its mistakes, so the lab that operates it is the natural party to answer. Reputation adds what monitoring lacks: a judge other than the seller, a cost for being wrong, and a reason to perform tomorrow. Standing must not be sold, and a failing unit must not restart under a new name. A basic record can be built now; a fully trustworthy one still needs proof that the readings are real, ground truth where agreement is not enough, a deeper validator pool, and privacy protection for donor cells. Feeding reputation back into the neurons is a research question, not a claim.

responds_to.name: Simon Sharwood, Inside datacenter where day starts with cerebrospinal fluid (The Register, 14 March 2026), reporting the launch of the Cortical Labs biological computing cloud
